html:
SMTO-GWT-0025 — The Gateway turned down this request

GUID: 6b510639-9edf-4682-b356-102025feb107
Slug: gateway-request-rejected
Domain: GWT · Subsystem: gateway

What happened

  • The Gateway received SMTO's request but answered with an error instead of doing it. Often nothing ran, but for some settings changes SMTO can't be sure.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open Technical details in this panel and read the Gateway's reason. The reason tells you whether the request was unsupported, not allowed, too large or failed for another reason.
  2. If the reason says the request isn't supported, open Settings › Setup › Gateways, select Check for updates, and update this Gateway. An older Gateway may not know how to do this kind of request yet.
  3. If you were changing a Gateway setting, reopen that setting and see whether your change is already there before saving it again. For settings changes SMTO can't be sure the Gateway ignored the request.
  4. If the reason mentions a size limit, try again with a smaller file or fewer items. The Gateway refuses requests that are bigger than it accepts.

What success looks like

  • The request completes and the Gateway shows the expected result, such as the saved setting or the sent email.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages the Gateway. Don't keep resending the same request unchanged; the Gateway will turn it down again.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The Gateway answered the request with an error status (forwarded from a Gateway settings call, or an email, file or privileged-command request); whether the request ran depends on which call failed and its response phase.

What this means

  • A Gateway request returned an HTTP rejection or error; specialized operation paths classify documented admission statuses, while the settings proxy forwards broader HTTP errors. The category alone does not prove pre-execution rejection. Use the retained operation phase and identity to determine effects; this explanation does not authorize retries or change pairing, target selection or execution ownership.

Why this can happen

  • A Gateway request returned an HTTP rejection or error; specialized operation paths classify documented admission statuses, while the settings proxy forwards broader HTTP errors. The category alone does not prove pre-execution rejection.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the endpoint, HTTP status, execution flags and retained phase before correcting fields or deciding whether further work is safe.

How to fix it

  • Read the HTTP status and detail in Technical details. On file and email operations, 400/404/405/422/501 means the Gateway build rejected or does not support the request before running it (update the Gateway). Errors forwarded by the Gateway settings proxy keep the Gateway's own status (for example 401/403 pairing or authorization, 409 conflict, 413 oversized request) and do not prove the change was not applied, so inspect the Gateway's current state before resubmitting a change.
  • Follow the structured status and rejection detail. Correct invalid fields only when supported; reconcile uncertain execution before submitting another mutation.

Retry and execution caution

  • Apply the correction and confirm the relevant state before requesting another attempt. Prior completed work remains governed by its receipts.

How to verify the fix

  • The indicated request defect is corrected, and any potentially started operation is reconciled before another mutation.

What not to do

  • Do not repeatedly submit the same invalid input; correct the named constraint first.

Technical notes

  • Use the retained operation phase and identity to determine effects; this explanation does not authorize retries or change pairing, target selection or execution ownership.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
